purpose: Complete the first nontrivial syndrome-compression rank. v5.9 classifies the projectively distinct rank-three zero-free simple-graphic case as K4. This artifact proves that every rank-three configuration with a repeated projective column direction necessarily has a signed zero on a simple graph. Therefore K4 is the complete simple-graphic rank-three zero-free classification.

setup.graph: G is simple with oriented incidence matrix B over GF(3).
setup.projection: A is a rank-three matrix with row(A) subseteq ker(B), for example A=H Q for a rank-three projection H of a full cycle matrix Q.
setup.sign_image: T(A)={A s : s in {+1,-1}^{E(G)}}. Zero columns are irrelevant and may be deleted from the support graph.
setup.projective_multiplicity: For each nonzero column direction L in PG(2,3), n_L is its multiplicity. Call L repeated when n_L>=2 and singleton when n_L=1.

repeated_block_lemma.statement: A repeated direction L can contribute any scalar multiple 0,+v_L,-v_L to the signed column sum. Hence all repeated directions together contribute their full linear span R in GF(3)^3.
repeated_block_lemma.proof: Two signed copies of any nonzero collinear column already realize the three scalar sums 0,+v,-v over GF(3); additional copies only translate within the same line. Contributions from different repeated lines add independently, giving exactly their span R.
repeated_block_lemma.quotient_reduction: Consequently 0 is absent from T(A) iff the signed sum of singleton columns never vanishes after projection to GF(3)^3/R. Singleton columns lying in R disappear in the quotient.

case_rank_R_3.proof: If rank(R)=3, repeated blocks can realize every vector in GF(3)^3 and therefore cancel the singleton contribution for any singleton sign choice. Thus 0 belongs to T(A).

case_rank_R_2.quotient: GF(3)^3/R is one-dimensional. Because rank(A)=3, at least one singleton column projects nonzero.
case_rank_R_2.one_dimensional_classification: A signed sum of k nonzero GF(3) scalars can avoid zero for every sign choice iff k=1. For k=2 choose opposite signs; for k>=3 an elementary sign choice gives residue zero, and the checker exhausts the finite residue recurrence.
case_rank_R_2.zero_free_abstract_shape: Exactly one singleton projective column e lies outside R; all other singleton columns lie in R.
case_rank_R_2.graphic_contradiction: Choose a nonzero linear functional phi annihilating R. Then phi A is a nonzero graph flow supported on exactly the one edge e. A loopless graph has no nonzero one-edge flow. Hence rank(R)=2 cannot be zero-free graphically.

case_rank_R_1.structure: All repeated columns lie on one projective direction L. Project modulo R=L to a two-dimensional quotient. The projected singleton columns occupy the four directions of PG(1,3), with quotient multiplicities caused by different PG(2,3) points on the same projective line through L.
case_rank_R_1.rank2_import: By v5.8, a rank-two sign image is zero-free only in abstract pattern I: exactly two quotient directions occupied and at least one has multiplicity one; or pattern II: all four quotient directions occupied exactly once.
case_rank_R_1.pattern_I_graphic_contradiction: Let D_s be a quotient direction of multiplicity one and D_o the other occupied direction. Choose a quotient linear functional vanishing on D_o but not D_s and lift it to phi on GF(3)^3 annihilating R. Then phi A is a nonzero flow supported on the unique edge in D_s, impossible in a loopless graph.
case_rank_R_1.pattern_II_graphic_contradiction: All four quotient directions occur once. The two-dimensional family {phi A : phi annihilates R} consists of two independent graph flows supported on exactly those four singleton edges. Thus the simple four-edge support subgraph would have cycle rank at least two. But every simple graph with four edges has cycle rank at most one. Contradiction.

complete_theorem.name: RANK3_ZERO_FREE_SIMPLE_GRAPH_SYNDROME_IFF_K4_CYCLE_SPACE_SUPPORT
complete_theorem.statement: Let A have rank three and row(A) lie in the GF(3) cycle space of a simple graph G. Then 0 is absent from A{+1,-1}^{E(G)} iff the nonzero-column support graph is K4 and row(A) is its full three-dimensional cycle space (up to an invertible change of syndrome coordinates).
proof: If a projective direction repeats, one of rank(R)=1,2,3 applies and the preceding cases force 0 into the sign image, contradiction.
Thus every zero-free graphic configuration has projectively distinct nonzero columns. v5.9 then forces its support graph to be K4 and its rank-three row space to equal the K4 cycle space.

Conversely, for the full K4 cycle space, A s=0 with s in {+1,-1}^6 would be a nowhere-zero GF(3) tension on K4. By the tension/colouring equivalence this would give a proper 3-colouring of K4, impossible. Hence the K4 cycle-space syndrome is zero-free.

positive: All sound rank-three linear syndrome UNSAT certificates on simple graphs are completely understood: they are exactly K4 cycle-space certificates.
A rank-three projection cannot encode a nonlocal obstruction larger than K4; repeated projective directions always reintroduce a false zero.
K4 detection plus a three-row cycle-space replay is a polynomial exact verifier for the entire rank-three certificate class.
killed: Search for a clever formula-dependent rank-three linear syndrome hash that certifies larger simple-graphic non-3-colourable cores without exposing a K4 support.
Hope that repeated projective column directions provide a new rank-three zero-reflecting pattern.
Use any rank-three projected zero-test as a universal substitute for the full linear-size cycle syndrome.
not_killed: Rank-four and higher source-certified linear syndrome projections.
Iterative contractions that remove recognized K4-like structures and then recompute the syndrome.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_RANK4_SYNDROME_OBSTRUCTION_CLASSIFICATION_V6_1
next_target.directive: Rank three is now exhausted and gives only K4. Move to rank four using PG(3,3) geometry only with aggressive quotienting by repeated directions; do not brute-force the full sign cube. First determine whether zero-free rank-four simple-graphic projections correspond to a finite family of 4-critical support graphs of bounded size or can already carry arbitrarily large obstructions. A useful theorem must provide a polynomial recognition/contraction rule or a sharp barrier.
